findings.detail: Issuer extraction is contaminated by schedule context and loan terms; the source issuer is the first-column company name, while the extracted row stores a long concatenated descriptor as issuer_name.

rationale: D06 is a class 3 continuity flag: the oracle reports only 41.4% issuer persistence (163/394), below the 50% threshold. The filing itself has March 31, 2025 and December 31, 2024 SOI tables with matching issuers, including Applied Digital Corporation in both periods. Raw source table 13 row 5 shows the current-period issuer as the first-column company name, and table 43 row 10 shows the same issuer in the comparative schedule. The bundle's extracted holdings sample instead stores issuer_name as a concatenated descriptor including schedule section, geography, industry, issuer, investment type, dates, rate, and EOT terms. That issuer-name extraction gap can mechanically depress issuer continuity despite source-visible persistence, so the flag represents a real data error rather than genuine portfolio turnover.
